title: How Lenny Rachitsky used high-quality writing and word of mouth to build a top newsletter
summary: Lenny explains how he went from a post-Airbnb Medium essay to a paid Substack newsletter that grows ~90% through word of mouth. He covers choosing topics by energy and curiosity, investing heavily in quality and research, using Twitter for distribution, and going paid and building a community.

principles.text: Follow the work that gives you energy and treat early content traction as a signal worth pursuing.
principles.quote: you should actually be spending more time on things that give you energy and less time on things that sap your energy

principles.text: Write what you are genuinely curious about, with audience input as a secondary signal; otherwise you rebuild a job you dislike.
principles.quote: the more interested i am in a thing i'm working on the better it gets and so i try to stay close to like just writing things i'm really interested in

principles.text: Quality wins in a sea of free content: time invested in a post correlates directly with how it performs.
principles.quote: the only way you stand out is you're better than all of those other ones like not just a little bit better but it's like oh wow this is so good

principles.text: Spend almost no time on distribution; great content spreads via word of mouth, and Twitter nuggets bootstrap the audience.
principles.quote: i think 90 of my growth is just word of mouth people sharing it with each other

principles.text: Build an audience by adding value in public (e.g. Twitter) first, then point it at your newsletter at launch.
principles.quote: find places to add value to people's lives and then you'll build the audience there over time

principles.text: Give away the best parts upfront in tweets and posts instead of building to a reveal.
principles.quote: the more you just give away all the good stuff quickly the better it does
